predecessors.name: Koch Bihar
predecessors.text: Raghudev's eastern portion of the Koch kingdom: Goalpara and Kamrup to the Barnadi and, bridged, the Barak Valley

successors.name: Mughal Empire
successors.text: Koch Hajo, from the Sankosh to the Barnadi

ledger.x: 1581: Raghudev, Chilarai's son, splits the kingdom at Barnagar near the Manas and takes the eastern portion.
After 1596: Raghudev moves the capital from Barnagar to North Guwahati.
July 1612: 'The Mughal army and navy began its expedition from near Dhaka in the July 1612.'
1613: the infobox dates the Mughal conquest of Kamrup to 1613; the Koch Hajo text has Parikshit driven up to Pandu in 1614, where he surrenders.
1613: Koch Hajo ends in the Mughal conquest of Kamrup.

wars.name: Raghudev's war with Koch Bihar and the Mughals
wars.outcome: 'The Koch Bihar-Mughal alliance defeated Raghudev in May 1597'; Lakshmi Narayan of Koch Bihar had submitted to Mughal vassalage in 1596.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of Koch Hajo
wars.outcome: Mughal forces, allied with Lakshmi Narayan of Koch Bihar, took Koch Hajo; Parikshit Narayan was sent to Delhi (Koch dynasty page) or surrendered at Pandu in 1614 (Koch Hajo page).

certainty.note: The pages give the Sankosh, Manas, Barnadi and Bhareli rivers as limits and no area; the shape is two discs round Goalpara and Kamrup and the Barak Valley as a bridge.
